To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we present a geo-distributed machine learning system, Gaia that (2) uses a new ML synchronization protocol, ASP, to (3) provide 1.8-53.5× faster ML training than state-of-the-art geo-distributed ML systems, and (4) is within 1.4× of the speed achieved by ML training on a LAN.
we present Gaia, a geo-distributed, ML system, that achieves high performance and is flexible enough to run different ML algorithms, without changing the algorithm.

we introduce Gaia, a general geo-distributed machine learning system that achieves LAN-like performance over WANs by decoupling intra-DC communication and inter-DC communication, and that we present a new ML consistency model, ASP, that enables Gaia to dynamically eliminate insignificant WAN communication while still guaranteeing ML algorithm correctness.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing ML systems that can scale to large numbers of data centers and WAN bandwidth constraints, while retaining the performance and accuracy of ML algorithms.

developing a geo-distributed system for ML that (1) efficiently utilizes scarce WAN bandwidth; (2) is flexible and can support a wide variety of ML algorithms; and (3) can run across multiple geo-distributed data centers, without requiring the ML algorithms to be changed.

the problem of developing a geo-distributed machine learning (ML) system that (1 ) employs an intelligent communication scheme over wide-area networks to efficiently utilize the limited WAN bandwidth, while still preserving the correctness guarantees of an algorithm; and (3 ) is generic enough to run a variety of ML algorithms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have developed a geo-distributed machine learning system that achieves LAN-like performance over WANs.

Gaia is a new ML system that can run ML algorithms across multiple data centers while retaining the accuracy guarantees and correctness of the algorithms, and is within a factor of 1.4x of the performance of the same algorithms running in a local area network.
Gaia is a general geo-distributed system that provides high performance, high availability, and scalability for ML algorithms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Gaia provides a general, flexible and scalable geo-distributed ML platform that can run a wide range ML algorithms over geo-distributed data, while achieving high performance and correctness guarantees.
we have developed a general geo-distributed machine learning system, called Gaia, that can be used to train machine learning models on large datasets distributed across multiple data centers.
we have developed a geo-distributed machine learning system that can run a wide range applications with minimal changes to the application and still achieve high throughput.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to achieve LAN-like ML system performance across multiple geo-distributed data centers.
it is possible to achieve LAN speed in a geo-distributed environment, without sacrificing the accuracy of the ML algorithm.

, with careful design and implementation of a distributed ML system, one can obtain ML system performance approaching LAN speeds even over WANs, while retaining the correctness and accuracy of ML algorithms.
